newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to mull fund raising for unification - minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to mull fund raising for unification - minister.

text.p: South Korea would study ways of raising funds to cover the huge cost of possible unification with the impoverished North, a government minister said on Thursday.

"We are considering consulting with the financial ministry about installing a unification fund because we acknowledge the issue cannot be postponed any longer," a ministry statement quoted National Unification Minister Kwon O-kie as telling a parliamentary session.
Kwon did not elaborate but it was the first time a senior government official has mentioned a special plan on unification costs.
The exact cost involved of unifying the two Koreas is unclear but experts estimate a range from 3.5 trillion won ($4.02 billion) to 1,800 trillion won, Yonhap Television News (YTN) said.
YTN said Kwon was bracing South Korea for a possbile collapse of the North.
North Korea has suffered from severe food shortages and economic difficulties, and the collapse of the Stalinist country has been predicted for many years.
The two Koreas remain bitter enemies and are technically still at war years after an armistice ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
The Korean peninsula was divided in the closing days of World War Two as advancing Soviet troops occupied the North and American troops the South.
North Korea, with most of the peninsula's natural resources and its industrial base, was the richer half at first but its relative wealth has eroded under four decades of Stalinist rule.
In contrast, South Korea emerged in the 1980s as one of Asia's fast-growing "miracle" economies. Last year its per capita income was $10,000 compared with $1,000 for the North.
Tensions on the Korean peninsula have been fanned by a string of North Korean defections, including Pyongyang's top ideologue who sought asylum last month in Seoul's diplomatic mission in Beijing.
